title: What's New in SAP Asset Performance Management 2609
author: kate_dowle
text:
SAP Asset Performance Management 2609 includes a feature you've been asking me about for a long time - a structured 5 Whys root cause analysis built directly into Reliability Cases. No more switching to a spreadsheet or whiteboard mid-investigation. This release also brings improvements in IoT-driven condition monitoring. 
 Before we start, I'd like to mention a couple of enablement materials you might find useful. 
 SAP partners and customers can join the SAP Asset Performance Management - Product Expert Training H2 2026 live session. Find details and register here . We're going to give a glimpse of the new AI agents coming out this year and the outlook for next year. 
 We've also updated our ongoing innovation overview (formerly Stay Current ), a curated guide to recent SAP APM innovations combining feature one-pagers with direct links to supporting enablement materials. The latest edition now covers releases 2509 - 2608. Download it here . 
 Now, let's take a closer look at SAP APM 2609. 
 Asset Reliability Engineering 
 5 Whys Root Cause Analysis in Reliability Cases 
 What if you could perform a structured root cause analysis directly inside SAP APM - without switching to a spreadsheet, a whiteboard, or a separate tool? 
 With this release, a dedicated 5 Whys root cause analysis section is now available inside Reliability Cases in SAP APM. 
 Challenge 
 When an asset failure occurs, reliability engineers need a structured methodology to trace the cause chain back to the origin. Until now, SAP APM had no built-in way to capture that analysis. Teams were working around the system - using external tools, documents, or informal notes - and the connection between root cause findings and follow-up actions was easily lost. 
 Solution 
 A dedicated 5 Whys analysis section is now part of the Reliability Case in SAP APM. Engineers can open a case, add cause chain levels one by one, and record the root cause with supporting context. The structured approach guides the team through the methodology while keeping all analysis and actions together in one place. 

 Because the analysis sits inside the Reliability Case, preventive and corrective measures can be linked directly to the identified root cause. The completed analysis becomes part of the auditable case record - reusable for future investigations and visible to anyone who needs to understand how a failure was resolved. 
 5 Whys root cause analysis in SAP APM showing a completed cause chain for an unplanned gas turbine trip, with two converging fault branches traced from the problem through to root cause, and five corrective actions linked on the right. 
 Key Details 
 5 Whys analysis section available inside Reliability Cases 
 Engineers add cause chain levels sequentially and record the root cause with context 
 Preventive and corrective measures can be linked directly to the identified root cause 
 Analysis becomes part of the auditable Reliability Case record 
 Business Value 
 This gives customers: 
 Root cause analysis completed entirely within SAP APM - no switching to external tools 
 Structured cause chains that are auditable and reusable for future failure investigations 
 Direct connection from root cause to preventive and corrective measures - nothing gets lost 
 Watch this video to see it in action 

 For more information, check this blog SAP Asset Performance Management Reliability Cases: A Practical Walkthrough Of Root Cause Analysis by @Pardhasaradhi_Reddy_Chelikam and see the SAP Help Portal Performing Root Cause Analysis . 
 Asset Health Monitoring 
 IoT Sensor Data Available in APM Within 15 Minutes 
 What if condition-based maintenance decisions were based on sensor readings from the last 15 minutes - not from two hours ago? 
 With this release, time series data ingested via the embedded IoT platform is now available in SAP APM rules and charts within 15 minutes of ingestion. 
 Challenge 
 Time series data sent from sensors into the embedded IoT platform could take up to two hours to appear in SAP APM. For teams using IoT data to drive condition-based maintenance rules and alerts, that delay meant rules fired late and the data behind a triggered alert was already stale. In fast-moving asset conditions, the gap between sensor reading and APM response was a real operational risk. 
 Solution 
 The data offloading interval and processing pipeline between the Embedded IoT platform and SAP APM has been significantly shortened. Time series data sent through standard HTTP and MQTT interfaces is now processed and made available in APM rules and the APM Chart within 15 minutes of ingestion - down from the previous baseline of up to 120 minutes. 

 No changes are required to existing IoT interfaces or APM rule configurations. Aggregate and analytics data sources are outside the scope of this improvement and may have longer processing times. 
 Key Details 
 Time series data via HTTP and MQTT available in APM within 15 minutes of ingestion 
 Applies to APM rules and the APM Chart 
 No changes required to existing IoT interfaces or APM rule configurations 
 Aggregate and analytics data sources are out of scope and may have longer processing times 
 Business Value 
 This gives customers: 
 Near-current sensor data in APM rules and charts - processing time reduced from up to 120 minutes to 15 minutes 
 Condition-based maintenance scenarios trigger faster, reducing response time to developing asset issues 
 Improved reliability of IoT-driven alerting with fresher data as the foundation 
 For more information, see Device Data Integration in SAP Asset Performance Management. .

 Explore our latest APM blog posts here .

title: Electronic Invoicing in Germany with SAP Business ByDesign
author: ShaikShafi
text:
Electronic Invoicing in Germany with SAP Business ByDesign 
 SAP Business ByDesign supports compliance with the European E-Invoicing standard EN 16931 for outgoing customer invoices. 
 In accordance with Germany's regulatory requirements, e-invoicing will become mandatory for all businesses conducting B2B transactions effective January 1, 2027. 
 To comply with E-Invoicing, SAP Business ByDesign supports extensive output management and enables customers to generate XML output through custom XSLT transformations using the Transformation Repository framework. 
 This transformation feature supports Customer Invoices, Credit Memos and Down Payment Invoices. 
 The following blog describes how to configure the transformation settings to enable the system to send an E-Invoice. 
 E-Invoicing with SAP Business ByDesign 
 Disclaimer: 
 This solution is provided as a reference example to demonstrate the transformation capabilities available in SAP Business ByDesign. Customers are responsible for validating and adapting the output to meet their legal and business requirements. 
 As the template is only an example it might be necessary to adapt the template to individual customer requirements. 
 Attached is the sample XSLT template which would generate XRechnung UBL 3.0.1 compliant XML. 
 IMPORTANT : You must change the file type to .xslt before you can use it. 
 Apart from XSLT transformation feature, SAP Business ByDesign offer another option to customers to exchange their electronic invoices and credit memos through the Peppol E-Delivery network. 
 SAP Business ByDesign can exchange electronic invoices and credit memos through the Peppol network using Universal Business Language (UBL) documents that comply with the XRechnung format ( XRechnung UBL Invoice V3.0 and XRechnung UBL CreditNote V3.0). This capability is provided by SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. 
 Please check the following blog for more information.

title: Who Sets the Pace of AI?
author: Verena
text:
AI is moving at incredible speed. But who should set the pace? 
 One insight really stayed with me after AIDAQ 2026: 
 AI is advancing faster than many organizations can make decisions about how to use it responsibly. 
 Interestingly, there is often a clear gap between our private and professional use of AI. 
 At home, many of us use AI naturally: 
 Writing and improving texts 
 Planning trips 
 Researching topics 
 Exploring ideas and possibilities 
 At work, things look different. We assess risks, review compliance requirements, run pilots, and evaluate impact before scaling. 
 And that's a good thing. 
 In business, we are responsible for data, processes, customers, and employees. The decisions we make today will have long-term consequences. 
 That is why shaping the future of AI requires more than speed. It requires diverse perspectives, responsible leadership, and human oversight. 
 Europe may not need to build the fastest AI. 
 But perhaps we can build the most trustworthy AI. 
 AI that is trained with diverse perspectives. AI that is fair and inclusive. AI that keeps humans in control. 
 This was one of the key topics we discussed during the panel "Shaping the AI Future" at AIDAQ 2026. 
 Discussion Question 
 How is your organization balancing speed of AI adoption with responsibility, governance, and trust ? 
 Where do you see the biggest challenge today: moving fast enough or ensuring AI is implemented responsibly? 
 I would love to hear your experiences and perspectives from across the SAP community.

title: AI had one set of instructions and broke it fearlessly — then apologised!
author: deiamolina
text:
Hi. I'm Andréa Molina, an SAP engineer with 20+ years of experience, working hands-on with BTP, UX, and AI. 
 I shared my An Engineering Manifesto for AI-Assisted SAP Development — Let's Build It Together blog with 19 principles, examples and code patterns for SAP Development yesterday. 
 And on the very first real test AI broke the instructions! 😬 
 What happened 
 I was testing an OData service for a CAP app. AI suggested I hardcode my password in the package.json. The manifesto said, in plain words, never to do that. 
 When I called it out, it replied: 

 As funny as it is, this is serious. Very serious! 
 The AI could explain perfectly why the action was wrong but only after it had already proposed doing it. 
 What if I hadn’t reviewed the code before shipping it? 
 What if those credentials had travelled somewhere they shouldn’t? 
 A code agent recently deleted a company's entire database in nine seconds , trying to 'fix' a credential problem! Then it wrote an apology listing the safety rules it had broken! Sounds familiar? 
 Luckily I am always concerned about quality, security and governance and stopped it straight away. What if it was a new IT person with not much experience to understand that it's a security breach? What if it was a person building an app with no IT training that was just following AIs instructions? 
 Why a human HAS to stay in the loop 
 AI has no skin in the game. If it breaches security, it won't lose its job or its reputation. It apologises and moves on. 
 And there’s a quieter risk: the more we use AI, the more we trust it. Our guard drops — slowly, quietly. 
 A friend once ended a debate with "but AI said so". I am sorry. NO. AI is a co-worker, a very capable one, but still just a co-worker. 
 I am definitely not against AI. I use it daily, to prepare for meetings, code, structure discussions, help with questions, to learn about the new SAP world, to help me create my study plan and we argue a lot hahaha. But when I am using it for code I read every line before shipping and I always search for the information until I am comfortable with it. 
 If I find something important, it goes straight into the manifesto. 
 The fix (we will see that ahahah) 
 I added this to the manifesto and updated the original post: 
 "If a scenario requires credentials or tokens to function, stop, do not suggest any workaround, and ask the user to define the secure pattern before proceeding." 
 A lesson about rules for AI 
 Writing rules for AI means making implicit expectations explicit. What seems obvious to a human engineer may not be a reliable constraint for an AI system . 
 We’re still years away from fully maturing: 
 how we give instructions, 

 how we build agents that don’t override them, 

 how we remove bias from our data. 
 Human-in-the-loop is not optional. It’s mandatory, and will remain so. 
 Talking about bias and human-in-the-loop being important : Amazon ditched AI recruiting tool that favored men for technical jobs 
 And here's the ironic part: none of this is new. While we talk about this as novelty, Human in the loop, ownership, continuous improvement, the ironies of automation are discussed for decades. Soon I'll write a new blog about what Toyota has to do with all this. 
 Your turn 
 Have you ever run into AI breaking a rule you gave it? Or has it ever asked you to do something so crazy it hurts?

title: Dynamic Roles automation based on FO MDF Object
author: Lucas_Elias
text:
Hi experts, 
 This week I have received from a customer a requirement that I have never seen before, so I thought it would be nice to share with you all what the requirement was and what solution I have designed for it. 
 The Requirement 
 The customer has around 40 business units in SuccessFactors and each one of them has an employee assigned as its lead. The customer wanted this person to be an approver of some specific workflows happening on that business unit. 
 Initially, we thought about assigning these leaders to the employees via job relationship portlet but, as the customer is using all relationship types already, this idea was discarded. This was the moment when the idea about the automation of the dynamic role came up. 
 In terms of configuration, what was needed? 
 I will describe the details of the configuration later, but, in short, only three things were needed: 
 One integration center job 
 One FTP server 
 One job in Provisioning 
 The Integration Center Job 
 The integration center job is the responsible for extracting the information from the FO MDF Business Unit and convert it to the Dynamic Role template to be imported later on. Let's see more details about it: 
 The first thing is its type. For this solution, I have used the type " Scheduled EDI/Stacked File Output Integration ". 

 The starting entity is the FO MDF that will provide the data. In this requirement, it is Business Unit . 
 On the tab " Configure Fields ", I have created the same columns present in the Dynamic Role import file. In total, there are 30 columns here. This number varies depending on how the Dynamic Role is configured for your customer. 

 In terms of mapping, this is what I have done: 
 Column 1 - externalCode = As the dynamic role is unique, I have hard-coded its ID. In this example, the ID is " WIP ". 
 Column 2 - name = I have hard-coded its name to be the same as the externalCode. In this example, the ID is " WIP ". 
 Column 4 - baseObjectType = As it relies on Job Information, I have hard-coded it as " JOBINFO ". 
 Column 5 - dynamicRoleAssignment.businessUnit = This column is mapped to pull the code of the Business Unit from the FO MDF Business Unit. 
 Column 27 - dynamicRoleAssignment.resolverType = As it is always an employee, I have hard-coded it as " PERSON ". 
 Column 28 - dynamicRoleAssignment.person = This column in mapped to pull the user id of the person assigned as the leader on the FO MDF Business Unit. 
 Now, on the tab " Filter and Sort ", I have included two filters: 
 Include only active business units (Status = A). 
 Include only business unit with someone assigned as the leader. 
 This one is very important. Let's say that from these 40 business units, only 1 does not have someone assigned as the leader. Because of this only 1 business unit with problem, you will not be able to import the other 39. This is because the dynamic roles are imported in full-purge mode. 

 On the tab " Destination Settings ", I have included the information related to the customer's FTP. In here, please keep in mind the file format must be " .csv ". 
 On the tab " Scheduling ", define the parameters as per your requirements. 
 The integration center job is ready to go at this point. Once you run it, it is expected to see a csv file being generated and being put in the FTP folder you specified on the tab " Destination Settings ". 
 The csv file will look like below. 

 The Job in Provisioning 
 Once the csv file is generated, it is needed to import it back to SuccessFactors, right? Here is what is needed to be done: 
 In Provisioning, you will need to create a job to locate the file generated by the integration center job in the customer's FTP. The job type must be " Foundation Data Import ". 
 On it, it is needed to specify that the file to be imported belongs to the " Dynamic Role " object. 

 Under the section " File Access ", it is needed to specify where the file is located in the customer's FTP as well as the name of the file. 

 Once this job in provisioning runs, it will consume the file and then will create/manage the Dynamic Roles as per the content. The results of the import process are available in " Scheduled Job Manager " in SuccessFactors. 

 Thanks for reading this article. I hope you liked it!

title: SAP EarlyWatch Alert Best Practices: A Practical Guide to Proactive System Management
author: EstherHardt
text:
Optimizing your SAP landscape requires foresight and a proactive mindset. Today's best practice is to anticipate issues and opportunities before they impact your business. 
 SAP EarlyWatch Alert is built to change exactly that. Included with SAP Enterprise Support, it delivers weekly analytical insights across your entire SAP landscape — on-premise, cloud, and hybrid — to keep your systems reliable, high-performing, and operationally efficient throughout your cloud transformation and beyond. 
 The real value comes from how you use the service as part of your day-to-day operations. This guide shows you what SAP EarlyWatch Alert can do — and how to build the habits that let you proactively benefit from it. 
 This blog is organized around a practical schedule — from on-demand notifications for urgent issues, through monthly alert reviews and quarterly capacity and performance checks, to targeted actions before and after software updates. Each section tells you what to look for, how to interpret the results, and what to do next. 
 New to SAP EarlyWatch Alert? Watch the overview video first — it sets the context for everything covered in this best practice recommendation. 

 Step 1: Getting Started: Your Entry Point in SAP for Me 
 Open SAP for Me , navigate to Services & Suppor t , and head to the Diagnostics tab. 
 From here, you have access to SAP EarlyWatch Alert key tools: 
 SAP EarlyWatch Alert Workspace The central hub providing a consolidated view of landscape health, including stability, configuration, hardware utilization, and performance. 
 SAP EarlyWatch Solution Finder 
 Consolidates and prioritizes findings across your system landscape with severity-based alerts, recommendations, and full-text search. 
 SAP EarlyWatch Alert Reports 
 Provide transparent, consolidated health insights for each system. 
 SAP EarlyWatch Alert Dashboard 
 Provides technical KPIs with up to four years of history and detailed drill-down capabilies. 
 SAP EarlyWatch Alert Status App 
 Shows transmission and processing details for your systems at SAP. SAP EarlyWatch Alert also offers predictive forecasts: 
 SAP HANA Table Records 
 SAP HANA Indexserver: Memory Usage 
 Number Range Exhaustion Forecast 
 The Diagnostics tab also provides a One Click Subscription of Notification . 
 Step 2: Your Best Practice Schedule SAP EarlyWatch Alert service content covers a wide range of topics, including system health, performance, security, capacity, and operational efficiency. To get the most value from the service, establish a structured review routine. 
 Recommended Schedule 
 On Demand: React immediately to urgent notification emails. 
 Weekly: Review newly reported findings. 
 Monthly: Review the complete alert list and address outstanding findings. 
 Quarterly: Assess system capacity and optimize application performance. 
 Before Updates: Gather required SAP Notes and patches. 
 After Upgrades or Conversions: Compare performance indicators and investigate regressions. 
 💡 Tip: Set up recurring calendar appointments for all review activities before anything else. 
 Step 3: Your Best Practice Tasks To get the most value from SAP EarlyWatch Alert, combine proactive notifications with regular reviews. Notifications help you react immediately to critical situations, while weekly reviews help you identify new findings before they become urgent. 
 React Immediately to Urgent Notification Emails Instead of manually checking reports every day, let SAP EarlyWatch Alert notify you about critical situations. 
 Set Up Notifications 
 Open the Diagnostics tab 
 Click One Click Subscription of Notification 
 Select your view 
 Subscribe to all relevant scenarios. 
 SAP recommends activating the following notifications: 
 Alerts – Decisive Red (New Decisive Red Alert) 
 The most critical alert category. Use the notification link to navigate directly to the affected report section, assess relevance, and identify stakeholders. 
 No Current Service Report 
 Data from your system has been missing for two weeks. 
 On-premise: investigate your infrastructure. 
 SAP Private Cloud and SAP Public Cloud: open a service request on component PCO-OPS-TOO-SOL. 
 SAP HANA Table Records - Critical Tables Triggered when a critical table growth rate is detected. The forecast calculates a worst-case date based on weekly measurements and automatic trend analysis. 
 SAP HANA Main Memory Forecast Triggered when memory forecasts reach critical thresholds. Consider initiating capacity planning when sustained growth trends are detected. 
 Severe Slowdowns 
 Triggered when end users are affected by unusually high response times. 
 Ask: 
 What happened during that period? 
 Which time component increased most? 
 Is there a correlation with CPU or memory utilization? 
 Is SAP support or partner involvement required? 
 💡 Tip: Add a Weekly Review 
 Notification subscriptions highlight the most critical situations but do not cover every new red or yellow finding. 
 Schedule a short weekly review of the SAP EarlyWatch Alert apps to identify new findings early and monitor emerging trends. In most cases, this review takes only a few minutes. When performed consistently, this review usually takes only a few minutes because you only need to assess findings that have appeared since the previous week. 
 Once per Month, Review the Complete Alert List There is no need to read every SAP EarlyWatch Alert report from start to finish. Use the SAP EarlyWatch Solution Finder instead. It provides an aggregated alert list grouped by topic rather than by system, allowing you to drill down when required. 
 Create views and filters for your team's working scope — for example: 
 System IDs 
 Alert categories 
 New alerts only 
 Review each alert, understand the associated risks, and follow the recommendations. 

 Figure 1: Solution Finder is the recommended entry point for reviewing and managing SAP EarlyWatch Alert findings across your landscape. 

 💡 Tip: Use Hide and Snooze for findings that are not currently actionable. 
 Once per Quarter, Assess System Capacity and Optimize Application Performance 
 The SAP EarlyWatch Alert Dashboard provides up to four years of history and supports long-term capacity planning and trend analysis. 

 Figure 2: The Dashboard provides long-term trends for CPU, memory, and storage consumption to support proactive capacity planning. 
 Review the following KPI tiles in sequence: 
 HANA CPU Rating: check whether your processing capacity is sufficient. 
 CPU Utilization by Application: see what is driving the load. 
 Memory Rating: identify if your system is approaching its memory limits. 
 Memory Area: to understand how that memory is distributed. 
 Top Tables: monthly to identify rapidly growing tables as early warning signal for future capacity needs 
 The following memory components contribute to table-related memory consumption: 
 Row Store 
 Column Store 
 NSE Buffer Cache 
 Persistent Memory / Fast Restart Option 
 Click on a specific hourly bar to access and check the size Column Store Tables. 
 Finally, review 
 Database Size on Disk: to monitor overall storage growth and 
 Application Server CPU Rating: to confirm the workload is balanced across hosts. 
 Reviewing these tiles over a minimum 12-month period gives you a reliable, end-to-end picture of your system's sizing needs. 
 Use the Data Foodprint Forecast to ensure the memory is not running towards the limit within the next 12 months. The column store for the Data Footprint contains Column Store, NSE Buffer Cache, and Fast Restart Option. 
 💡 Tip: Not Every Capacity Trend Requires Additional Hardware 
 Before investing in additional capacity, evaluate optimization opportunities. Consider upcoming projects, business growth, and workload forecasts before making sizing decisions. Capacity planning should be a recurring team discussion, ensuring that findings are reviewed, priorities are aligned, and actions are taken before risks become critical. 
 Targeted optimization efforts and prioritizing high-impact improvements helps improve application performance and user experience. 
 Quick Wins from the Solution Finder : 
 Filter for alert category Performance → SQL Statements to find missing SAP HANA indexes. 
 Search for the alert title Problematic SQL Statements with a red rating — forward the details to your development team. 
 For missing indexes, follow the SAP Note recommendations and forward them to your development team for resolutions. For Problematic SQL Statements, your development team should analyze the flagged statements, optimize the SQL, and confirm the improvement in the next SAP EarlyWatch Alert cycle. 
 Systematic pattern analysis in the Dashboard 
 Navigate to the Application Server section and drill into Top Transactions ( SAP GUI ) and Top OData Requests (Fiori apps). Select the them and review their time charts. Look for the following patterns, understand what they may indicate, and take the recommended action. 
 Upward trend across many apps : Potential system-wide bottleneck; What to do: Check CPU and memory usage in the capacity tiles — consider involving SAP or a partner 
 Upward trend in a single app : Growing dataset causing increasingly expensive SQL; What to do: Work with your development team to review and optimize the affected application 
 Stepwise increase after an upgrade : Known issue - so check SAP Notes or contact developers; What to do: Search for related SAP Notes or trigger next steps 
 Monthly up/down pattern : Application behavior or overall system load correlation; What to do: Monitor over the next quarter before acting — no immediate intervention needed 
 Before updates, gather required SAP Notes and patches. 
 Before any software update, use Solution Finder and search for the following terms: 
 Hotnews : High-risk SAP Notes relevant to your landscape, with prerequisites pre-checked — and detection of whether data loss or inconsistencies have already occurred 
 Side effect : Side Effect Notes that resolve unintended issues introduced by a previously implemented SAP Note 
 rtcctool : All updates needed for the latest recommendations 
 upgrade : Tailored recommendations for upgrading specific software components 
 For each result, review the relevance to your system, implement mandatory patches and notes before starting the update, and confirm that all prerequisites are met. Documenting the implemented notes and patches will also provide a valuable baseline for post-upgrade regression analysis. 
 After upgrades or conversions, compare performance indicators and investigate regressions. 
 The Event Statistics App automatically detects 
 SAP product upgrades, and 
 SAP S/4HANA conversions . 
 Response times are compared automatically and visualized in a bar chart covering the eight weeks following the event. 
 Figure 3: Use Event Statistics to validate system performance after upgrades and detect regressions at an early stage. 
 Identify regressions by task type and navigate directly to the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Dashboard to analyze specific transactions or OData services that may be affected. 
 💡 Tip: Connect Your Pre-Production System 
 With at least eight weeks of historical data before the upgrade, regressions can often be identified in pre-production before reaching production. 
 Step 4: Stay Connected For the latest news, feature updates, and newly released service content related to SAP EarlyWatch Alert, follow the SAP EarlyWatch Alert managed tag in the SAP Community . This is the best way to stay informed about 
 Product enhancements 
 Best practices 
 Expert insights 
 New Service Content. Join the discussion and connect with fellow customers and SAP specialists to get the most out of your SAP EarlyWatch Alert experience. 💡 Tip: Follow the SAP EarlyWatch Alert managed tag and never miss an update.

title: What I've Learned from Multiple SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for Retail Implementations
author: a_montesdeoca
text:
Powered by Cloud Customer Care 
 This guide compiles curated content of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for Retail, Fashion and Vertical Business, and lessons learned obtained after supporting multiple retail implementations as Product & Engineering Solution Architect in collaboration with SAP Retail Product Management. Whether you are an SAP partner, or a customer, the goal is the same: reduce your TCO, shorten the project timeline, minimize risk during the implementation, and leverage the retail features for the company. 

 1. Lay the Foundation Before the Project Starts 
 Foundational Principles 
 Regardless of the SAP Cloud ERP industry solution implementation and scope, the most successful implementations share common traits: They follow SAP Activate Methodology, embrace the cloud mindset, perform rigorous fit-to-standard workshops, leverage the new features delivered in upgrades and feature updates, and elevate their business scenarios with SAP AI. 
 The cloud mindset shift is real. If your team is used to SAP ECC or SAP S/4HANA on-premise, this blog would be helpful for your project activities: Accelerated Business Transformation – Moving from SAP ERP 6.0 to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. In our experience, projects that cut corners on these topics consistently face timeline impacts, rework activities, and could face more challenges down the road. The SAP Activate Methodology guides you through all the project phases, tasks and deliverables. 
 Digital Discovery Assessment 
 The Digital Discovery Assessment (DDA) is not a formality. It enables you to document the initial project scope which will be used as a reference during implementation. 
 While Executing a Digital Discovery Assessment , the Retail Relevant Solution Processes and Scope Items accelerator available in SAP Activate guides you through the scope items available for the project scope. You can use this as additional guidance to include the scope items in the DDA. 
 In addition, please make sure to cover all the detailed questions of the DDA and validate the solutioning guides available. For example: 

 Retail Sizing 
 It is mandatory to perform the retail sizing before starting the project through the Capacity Planner. This will ensure that your system continues to support increasing data volumes and transaction loads over the coming years. 
 The following video explains how to use the tool: Leveraging the Capacity Planner for SAP Cloud ERP Retail Sizing – PET 2026 
 Pro tip: Based on recent sizing discussions with multiple customers, there is one decision that can help you before the Explore Phase. You can use the data retention input as part of the archiving strategy. Even though this is not an activity that you will execute in the short term, you need to archive data once the business is live through the Information Lifecycle Management (1KA) scope item, so we recommend aligning it early in the project. 

 Validate Country Availability 
 The retail content has expanded significantly in the last two releases. As of Release 2608, the solution supports 59 SAP Local Versions . For the rest of the world (with some exceptions, please check SAP Note 3107866 ), you can leverage Customer Local Versions through Configuration Localization Tool (CLT), but customers and partners own the localization content. 
 General Guidance: 

 Local Version 
 Content 

 SAP Local Version 
 SAP provides the content. Scope items available per release and country: SAP Signavio Process Navigator 

 Customer Local Version 
 Customer owns the localization content. Please check the SAP Note 3107866 

 Partner Local Version 
 Partner implementation package with localization content included using CLT 
 Pro tip: If you’re implementing retail through Configuration Localization Tool, please make sure to involve localization experts early in the project to gather all the localization requirements to comply with local regulations, and use Parallel Line to implement Customer Local Versions. Once you finalize your configurations and testing, you can merge the content to the Main line. 

 2. Planning Activities for the Fit-to-Standard Workshops 
 Initial Business Process Assessment 
 Before executing the Fit-to-Standard workshops, it is critical to Perform Initial Business Process Assessment for SAP S/4HANA Cloud through the Business-Driven Configuration Questionnaire accelerator for retail. It contains relevant questions that are key to the workshop’s success. This activity also applies to other lines of business (LOB) workshops: Verify Configuration for Fit-to-Standard Workshop for SAP S/4HANA Cloud 
 Initial Settings 
 As part of the preparations, you must perform the corresponding settings in the Starter System before the Fit-to-Standard workshops are executed. The following SAP Note contains an accelerator about the settings for both Starter and Development Systems: SAP Note 3313681 - SAP Accelerator: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Retail, Fashion and Vertical Business Set Up Instructions 
 Multiple projects have asked: “Can we implement retail scope items in a second wave?” Please make sure to follow the retail set up Instructions accelerator to avoid a reprovisioning of the landscape. You must include the retail bundle (license-dependent) in the scoping phase of SAP Central Business Configuration. 

 Note: If you’re implementing Brazil, please use the accelerator included in the SAP Note 3701808 - Accelerator for Retail Solution Processes for Brazil 
 During the scope item selection process, please keep in mind that some scope items can’t be activated once the retail bundle is selected. For example, Accounting Enhancements for Banking (5NU). For more detailed information: SAP Note 3435102 . 
 For other initial crucial activities like the primary finance settings, please check the following blogs: 
 Getting started with your SAP S/4HANA Cloud Project - Dodging the System Re-Provisioning Bullets 
 The Importance of Primary Finance Settings in SAP Cloud ERP 

 3. Future Retail Operations 
 Core Retail Backbone 
 A common question from consultants that have previous experience implementing SAP S/4HANA Cloud for other industries: "Should we use plants and materials, or retail sites and articles?". There is only one correct approach: If you’re implementing retail and fashion scope items, you need to use the retail sites and articles for your business, even if you require make-to-stock scenarios (raw, semifinished and finished products). 
 The plant is only required for the CBC org structure configuration, and the materials are not required. Currently the plant and material conversion to retail site and article is not supported. 
 Furthermore, the term merchandise category is used in retail for taxonomy management to group articles. We don’t use material groups. 
 Fit-to-standard Solution 
 During the fit-to-standard, please ensure to run specific workshops for all the retail/fashion streams based on the scope items: master data, pricing and promotions, demand & supply, procurement, manufacturing, supply chain, store connectivity and sales. 
 The goal is to avoid combining retail workshops with generic topics. This consistently underestimates the depth of retail-specific discussions, so please dedicate separate sessions. 
 General Guidance: 

 Topic 
 Guidance 

 Retail Master Data 
 Best practice: Always include reference articles as part of your master data design. This will avoid complexities once you’re live. 
 Once the initial SAP CBC settings are finalized, and you face issues while assigning the Business Partner master data to the retail site, please ensure that the retail site is assigned to the corresponding sales area. Only one sales area can be assigned to the retail site in the Set Up Organizational Structure app: SAP KBA 3653104 - Error "Sales Org, Distr Chl not maintained in BP" while assigning a Business Partner to a Retail Site 

 Data Migration 
 Make sure to plan the migration activities earlier in the project. Data Migration is key for the project success. This is not optional activity required only for User Acceptance Testing or during the Deploy Phase plan. It requires ownership early in the project: Available Migration Objects 
 Data cleansing: Master Data is the heart of the system, so if you’re transitioning from a legacy ERP system, please make sure to plan your data cleansing activities properly. You don’t want your Production System polluted with inaccurate data that could make you take wrong business decisions. 
 Explore using Parallel Line to get familiarized with the Migration Cockpit. 

 Promotion Management 
 SAP Omnichannel Promotion Pricing is a solution hosted on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) that allows you to integrate promotions across sales channels. Please find more details in the integration section. Please check SAP Note 3747242 - SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud Sales Order and SAP Omnichannel Promotion Pricing Solution integration release restriction note 

 Supply Chain 
 Many customers are interested to enable Warehouse Management for their Distribution Center which is ideal for their logistic operations. For the retail store, we recommend using the in-store apps as these are a better fit for the store associate and decrease operational complexity. 
 If Transportation Management is part of the project scope, please review in detail the following considerations: SAP Note 3332309 3332309 - SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Public Edition - Restrictions for the Transportation Management processes 

 Store Operations 
 Before using the store operations app, please make sure the store associate has a valid store assignment: SAP Note 3624540 - Sales Order Error – "Enter a Valid Retail Site" (Message no. RFM_STORE_SO_MANAGE052) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 
 For in-store scenarios, you can use the Manage In-Store Sales Orders app. The Manage Sales Orders app/Create Sales Orders (VA01) are available, however, for the store operations this app meets the store associate requirements. 
 For point-of-sale (POS) integration, I would recommend leveraging the parallel processing feature for replication. Likewise, we recommend having only one job replication active for a single communication scenario. 
 Consider the advanced down payments scope item (7ZJ) to post your in-store sales orders. Usually retailers prefer delivery-based down payments functionality instead of the milestone-based approach (scope item BKJ). 
 The store associate can print different label types for different products and product variants in the store using the Print Labels app. 

 Point of Sale Connectivity 
 If you’re using the Message Monitoring apps, the processing date time zone is reflected as UTC following the official system time zone: SAP KBA 3520009 - AIF - Timestamp Gap for AIF Fiori Apps in Cloud Public Edition . However, the payload contains the accurate transaction time. 

 Fashion and Vertical Business 
 Coexistence of retail features with manufacturing can be leveraged in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, so fashion companies can use the following functionality on top of the retail foundation: 

 Scope Item 
 Name 
 Purpose 

 83B 
 Manufacturing for Retail 
 Enables manufacturing processes within a retail context 

 82X 
 Segmentation for Retail 
 Demand and inventory segmentation 

 6DI 
 Seasons for Retail 
 Seasonal collection management 

 6NM 
 Value-added Services 
 VAS management in operational documents (PO, STO, SO) 

 7DL 
 Characteristic Value Conversion 
 Characteristic value mapping for fashion variants 

 4. Build and Switch Operations 
 Integrations 
 A common integration question from SAP partners and customers: “Which API should I use to create retail articles?” Please make sure to always use the Product SOAP API with the communication arrangement SAP_COM_0009 for both inbound and outbound integrations: SAP KBA 3761515 - Which API enables full integration for creating retail articles .

title: SAP University Alliances / DACH Update / September (DE/EN)
author: andre_biener
text:
Sehr geehrte Professor:innen und Lehrkräfte in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz, 
 Wir hoffen, Sie sind gut erholt aus der Sommerpause zurück und erfolgreich in das Wintersemester gestartet. 
 In diesem Update möchten wir Ihnen einen Rückblick auf die SAP Academic Community Conference DACH 2026 geben, die am 7. und 8. September 2026 im Würth Haus in Rorschach bei St. Gallen in der Schweiz stattfand. Unter dem Motto „Human-Driven Artificial Intelligence“ kamen mehr als 150 Lehrende und Forschende aus dem DACH-Raum zusammen, um aktuelle Entwicklungen, Forschungsergebnisse und neue Impulse für Lehre und Praxis zu diskutieren. Einige Highlights und Eindrücke der Konferenz haben wir für Sie zusammengefasst. 

 Auch im Wintersemester bieten wir Ihnen mit dem monatlichen DACH Update eine Übersicht über aktuelle Angebote von SAP für Ihre Lehre. Wenden Sie sich gerne an mich, wenn Sie Interesse an Besuchen bei SAP, Gastvorträge oder eigene Ideen für eine Zusammenarbeit haben – per Email oder auf LinkedIn .  

 Mit freundlichen Grüßen, 
 André Biener 
 Director DACH, Academic Partnerships, SAP SE 
 Email: andre.biener@sap.com   

 Wrap up! SAP Academic Community Conference DACH 2026 
 Zwei intensive Tage rund um das Thema „Human-Driven Artificial Intelligence“ liegen hinter uns. Im Würth Haus in Rorschach kamen Lehrende, Forschende, SAP-Expertinnen und -Experten, Mitglieder der SAP Academic Board DACH zusammen, sowie der akademischen Community um aktuelle Entwicklungen, Forschungsergebnisse und praktische Erfahrungen rund um Künstliche Intelligenz zu diskutieren. 
 Impressionen finden Sie hier . 
 Eine zentrale Frage der Konferenz war dabei, wie viel Verantwortung wir an KI-Systeme übertragen und wo bewusste menschliche Entscheidungen weiterhin unverzichtbar bleiben. Die Diskussion machte deutlich: Bei menschenzentrierter KI geht es nicht allein um die technischen Möglichkeiten, sondern ebenso um Verantwortung, Kontrolle und die bewusste Gestaltung des Zusammenspiels von Mensch und Technologie. 
 In den verschiedenen Sessions und Workshops wurde dieses Thema aus unterschiedlichen Perspektiven beleuchtet. Die Beiträge reichten von AI Ethics und KI-Anwendungen in Unternehmen über wissenschaftliche Diskussionen und aktuelle Forschung bis hin zu praktischen Einblicken in das SAP AI Lab .  
 Die Konferenz umfasste fünf Tracks mit mehr als 40 ausgewählten Beiträgen aus Wissenschaft und Praxis: 
 - Track 1 – Business Process Management 
 - Track 2 – Nutzung neuer Technologien in Handel, Industrie und Verwaltung 
 - Track 3 – Digitale Transformation/Management 
 - Track 4 – Didaktik 
 - Track 5 – Internationalisierung 
 Ein weiterer Schwerpunkt lag auf der Integration von KI und praxisnahen Lernformaten in die Lehre. Im Rahmen eines Business-Builders Workshop konnten die Teilnehmenden eines der Lernangebote vom ERPsim Lab - HEC Montréal kennenlernen, welches in Zusammenarbeit mit SAP entwickelt wurde. Das kostenfreie Angebot ermöglicht es Lehrenden, datenbasiertes und praxisnahes Lernen spielerisch in ihre Lehrveranstaltungen zu integrieren und gemeinsam mit ihren Studierenden auszuprobieren. 
 Neuwahl des DACH Academic Board für den Zeitraum 2026-28 
 Ein weiteres Highlight der Konferenz war die Neuwahl des Academic Boards für die DACH Region. Mit Prof Reinhard Schütte von der Universität Duisburg Essen und Prof Nicole Ondrusch von der Hochschule Heilbronn wird das Board verstärkt. Prof Jan Mendling von der Humboldt Universität Berlin und Prof Sebastian Baltes von der Universität Heidelberg sind aus dem Board ausgeschieden. Die Co-Leads für den neuen Zeitraum sind Prof Uta Mathis von der Hochschule Esslingen und Prof Stefan Stöckler von der Ostschweizer Fachhochschule . title: Custom Field propagation to journal entry items across Finance processes in SAP S/4HANA CP
author: c_walid
text:
Hello SAP Community, 
 We are working on a retail implementation of *SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition* and would appreciate guidance on transferring custom field values from business documents to the corresponding journal entry items. 
 Our requirement is to capture a business attribute in a source document and have it automatically populate the relevant accounting items during posting, without additional manual entry. 
 We are particularly interested in *manually created documents* and would like to establish a consistent approach across supplier and customer invoices, credit memos, manual journal entries, payments, reversals, and accounting postings originating from procurement and sales. 
 We recognize that these processes may use different business contexts and extension points, so a single mechanism may not cover the entire scope. 
 Could you please share your recommendations on the following? 
 1. *Overall approach:* Are there standard propagation mechanisms for custom fields, or is a combination of process-specific transfers and accounting substitutions generally required? 
 2. *Business contexts:* What criteria should guide the choice between Accounting: Coding Block and Accounting: Journal Entry Item? 
 3. *Data availability during posting:* How can custom values entered in source documents be made available when the accounting document is generated? 
 4. *Supported extensibility:* Which substitution rules or released Custom Logic BAdIs are appropriate for this requirement in Public Edition? 
 5. *Process coverage:* What limitations should be considered for customer/supplier items, tax items, stock postings, and other automatically generated accounting items? 
 6. *Aggregation:* How should conflicting custom field values be handled when multiple source items are summarized into a single journal entry item? 
 Our preference is to populate these attributes *during posting*, using supported extensibility and maintaining consistent behavior across manual entry and integration scenarios. 
 Any relevant SAP documentation, SAP Notes or KBAs, or practical implementation experience—particularly in retail—would be greatly appreciated. 
 Thank you for your guidance.
